items.q: Which way do magnetic field lines point?
items.correct: From the north pole to the south pole outside the magnet.
items.misconception: From south to north outside the magnet.
items.random_wrong: There are no field lines unless two magnets are present.
items.why: By convention field lines run N → S outside a magnet (the way a free north pole would move); a single magnet still has a field.

items.correct: No — only iron, steel, nickel and cobalt are magnetic materials.
items.misconception: Yes, all metals are attracted to magnets.
items.random_wrong: Only gold and silver are magnetic.
items.why: Metals like aluminium and copper are not magnetic. The magnetic (ferromagnetic) materials are iron, steel, nickel and cobalt.

items.q: How can you make an electromagnet stronger?
items.correct: Increase the current, add more turns to the coil, or add a soft-iron core.
items.misconception: Use a longer wire but change nothing else.
items.random_wrong: Only swap to a higher-voltage battery.
items.why: Field strength depends on current, number of turns and the core; more turns and current plus a soft-iron core all increase it.
